name: Dodo
overview: Dodo was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, known primarily as the father of Puah. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond this familial connection. His mention in Judges 10:1 situates him within the genealogical and tribal context of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Dodo is a proper name meaning "beloved," though it was not given by God. This name reflects a personal designation found in the Scripture without additional titles or divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Dodo as the father of Puah, establishing a direct paternal relationship. He is also identified as a descendant of Issachar, linking him to this specific tribe of Israel. No other family relationships are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Dodo's significance in the biblical narrative rests on his role as the father of Puah and his tribal identity within Issachar. His mention helps to trace the lineage and leadership within Israel during the period recorded in Judges. Though not a central figure himself, his place in the genealogical record contributes to the broader understanding of Israel's tribal history.
